messages:
Anna L.: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to decide how operator-level permissions interact with project-scoped API keys.
Eli: tl;dr: either we treat operator perms as an overlay (can always escalate) or we namespace keys strictly by project. tradeoffs: simplicity vs least-privilege.
Maria: overlay is convenient for SRE runs, but it's a footgun for scripts that accidentally use operator keys. we should prefer least-privilege defaults. :warning:
Josef: agree on defaults, but we need a clear escape hatch for oncall. maybe timebound operator tokens (short TTL + MFA) rather than permanent overlay.
Anna L.: good idea — timebound operator tokens address safety. also need to define how service-to-service calls propagate identity: do we pass original API key, or mint ephemeral actor tokens?
Eli: minting ephemeral actor tokens is better for auditing and revocation, but it adds a small latency and infra complexity (token broker).
Maria: latency measured: ~8-12ms add if broker in-path, or we can async mint and cache for 60s. still worth it for TTL + traceability.
Josef: policy model question — do we keep RBAC at role-id level or move to capability predicates? role-id is easy to reason about; capability predicates are flexible but harder to audit across orgs.
Anna L.: i'd vote for hybrid: role-ids as primary surface for users + scoped capability predicates for infra-only gates. keep role->capability mapping centralized.
OpsSam: from ops side, we need tooling: 1) list keys by effective scope, 2) dry-run eval for a token (what can it access), 3) audit timeline. can we expose that in console?
Maria: yes, Console can show effective scopes and last-used timestamps. needs backend support: compute effective scope = union(project, org, overlays) + active operator-tokens.
Eli: edge: resource-level scoping (per-model, per-route) — do we allow resource wildcards in API keys? i'd limit wildcards to trusted service keys only. user keys default to project-only.
Josef: migration plan for existing long-lived keys: detect keys used across projects -> flag for rotation -> offer split wizard that creates per-project keys and maps usage patterns.
Anna L.: compatibility: keep a compatibility mode where old keys get a transitional policy but auto-expire in 90 days unless owners confirm.
Maria: question about header surface: keep Authorization: Bearer <token> but add X-Actor: <ephemeral-id> for minted cases so logs link original caller and brokered actor. example:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_...
X-Actor: actor_ebf23c4b
```
Eli: will that break existing proxies that scrub unknown headers? maybe we rely on structured logs and tracing instead, but X-Actor is handy. we should fallback to embedding actor in JWT claims.
Josef: good call — prefer JWT claim "act" and keep X-Actor as optional convenience header for internal proxies.
OpsSam: SLA question: if token-broker is down, do we fail closed or allow fallback? we should fail closed for sensitive ops, allow cached tokens for reads. document fallback policy.
Anna L.: next steps: create a short RFC PR with: 1) operator token TTL proposal, 2) token-broker sketch (mint/cache/rehydrate), 3) hybrid RBAC/capability model, 4) migration strategy for existing keys, and 5) audit/console requirements.
Maria: I'll volunteer to draft the console requirements. Eli/Josef can do broker sketch. Anna, can you draft the operator TTL + migration?
Anna L.: yep, I'll start a PR today. tagging @security-bot to add an action item and remind in 1 week. :white_check_mark:
security-bot: created task SEC-7894 "AuthZ operator-perimeter RFC PR" assigned to Anna L., Maria, Eli, Josef due 7 days.
Eli: tiny nit — include example policy JSON for capability predicates in the PR so reviewers have something concrete.
Josef: also include a small compatibility test plan: smoke that checks per-project key denial for out-of-scope resource.
Anna L.: noted. thanks all — closing this thread, will post PR link when ready.
